pre_text:
Hello again, peeps. We're all set. The rain has stayed away. May it remain that way for we all want a cracker. Huge cheers as Kohli & Faf walk out to open the batting. Tushar Deshpande to bowl the first over. A slip in place for him. Kohli to face the first ball.





7.20pm Shashank is back to see you through the first innings. Let him know whom you are cheering for tonight, even if it's for some rain!

Aashish Pudasai: "Come on RCB. It is do or die game. Supporting you from Nepal"

CSK: 1 Ruturaj Gaikwad (capt), 2 Rachin Ravindra, 3 Daryl Mitchell, 4 Ajinkya Rahane, 5 Mitchell Santner, 6 Ravindra Jadeja, 7 MS Dhoni (wk), 8 Shardul Thakur, 9 Maheesh Theekshana, 10 Tushar Deshpande, 11 Simarjeet Singh. Impact Subs: Dube, Rizvi, Solanki, Rasheed and Choudhary

RCB: 1 Faf du Plessis, 2 Virat Kohli, 3 Glenn Maxwell, 4 Rajat Patidar, 5 Cameron Green, 6 Dinesh Karthik, 7 Mahipal Lomror, 8 Yash Dayal, 9 Karn Sharma, 10 Mohammed Siraj, 11 Lockie Ferguson. Impact Subs: Swapnil, Rawat, Prabhudesai, Vyshak and Himanshu

7pm Like most of us, Ravi Shastri is right on the top of his voice at the toss. CSK win the toss and bowl. The thrill in the crowd is unbelievable, even as Gaikwad somehow manages to be audible and say the cloud cover is one of the reasons for his decision. CSK play Santner in place of Moeen. Faf du Plessis would have bowled first too. Remember, RCB have won five in a row to leave themselves with a fair chance of qualifying for the playoffs.

Amit: "Please start early as it is not raining" --- Is someone listening or reading?!

Somesh: "@Himanshu- who are you supporting today. Don't say rain please" --- Okay, I'm all for some exciting cricket then!

Anil: "Himanshu, please answer the MOST important question today: by what margin must RCB win today to push CSK aside? CSK has higher NRR" --- It is S Rajesh, and not me, who has all the answers

Meanwhile, Ashish says all signs lead to Richard Gleeson coming back. He has been practising for a while.

Shekhar: "Considering there's a mega auction coming up, the sensible thing to do for Dhoni would be to retire. But hey, I thought the same 3 years back, so, huh, whatever" --- Why do we even think when it comes to Dhoni?!

Ashish Pant from Chinnaswamy: Dhoni just walked out to a wild roar from the crowd, but he's walked in very late. Probably the last man to walk out of the CSK unit. The suspense builds because Avanish Aravalley has been practising for the last 10-15 minutes to almost all the fast bowlers. Dhoni struts out and immediately walks over to his teammates who are doing some football drills. Chants of Dhoni, Dhoni rings around the stadium.

Hello, everyone. Who hasn't lost patience yet for the action to begin?

Himanshu Agrawal is ready to step in with the controls for a short while. I'll see you very soon.

6.35pm  Is this the sternest test yet for Ruturaj Gaikwad?  His first year as CSK captain has fetched mixed results so far. Not once have CSK won more than two games in a row this season, not once have they lost more than two on the bounce. Now it all boils down to one pressure game.

There's so much chatter around this potentially being MS Dhoni's final IPL game. Well, never say never. The one thing with Dhoni is you don't quite know what surprise he'll pull off when. Even Mike Hussey isn't sure.

 6.20pm  Halfway through the season, almost no one gave RCB a chance of making the playoffs. But they are still here, having strung together a run of wins in what was effectively five knockout games. Hopefully, the weather in Bengaluru will allow them their shot at completing the greatest comeback in IPL history.




Abhilash: "I think you'll copy and paste these two lines much often - 1. Covers are coming off 2. Covers are back on." -- Hahaha, yeah entirely possible it could be that kinda evening.


6.05pm  Covers are coming off.








Ravim says: "It would have been better had it rained till now and cleared the hovering clouds. No rain till now is not a good news. It may mean rain may hit us during match "


5.56pm Covers are coming on.  I presume this is just a precautionary measure because there is some rain forecast around now.


5.55pm  One of the big reasons for RCB's turnaround has been Rajat Patidar. Colleague S Sudarshanan caught up with him a couple of days to go to chat about his batting, season, spin-hitting and a bit more.


Walt: "Bright, early start to the commentary! Perhaps the IPL could be un-cricket like and start early, to take advantage of the weather...? " -- Spot on, Walt. Cricket should be less rigid.








S Rajesh, our stats editor, breaks down the simple equation for RCB & CSK.


5.40pm  So far, we had only heard murmurs of people being approached to become India's next head coach. We can confirm one candidate for sure now. Any guesses? 


BTW, last time RCB-CSK played on May 18, this happened. Check it out.


5.30pm  Good evening, folks. Who would've imagined even probably two weeks ago that this fixture - RCB v CSK - would be a knockout (well, almost).

"Oh, man. Absolute chaos outside the Chinnaswamy," belts Ashish Pant, our reporter at the venue tonight. Presume he's referring to the traffic. Because we can confirm IT. IS. NOT. RAINING.

On that note, hello and welcome to our coverage of Match No. 68. Fondly, and in a banter-y sort of manner, referred to as the Cauvery derby. If you understand southern politics, you'd probably pick up the reference. 

I'm Shashank Kishore, welcoming you all. Stay locked. I'll bring you just about anything and everything as it happens. Including who moved, who waved, who burped.....okay, that's me getting overly excited. I'll relax.

pre_text:
We're set to resume. Theekshana into the attack


8.15pm  The main covers are coming off. Play to resume at 8.25pm. No overs lost.


Elsewhere, how does an Olympic lifter train to lift 244 times her bodyweight? Mirabai Chanu routinely lifts 12000kg a day as practice - Virat Kohli would need to face 10000 deliveries to lift the same weight. It seems impossible but she's doing it just months after she needed a wheelchair. Her next goal - a second Olympic medal at Paris 2024.








Ashish Pant from Chinnaswamy: Mop up operations are underway. Kohli and Faf have walked down to the dug out from the dressing room. Chinnaswamy's sub-air aeration system has already worked its magic. It absolutely pelted down, but there is no water on the outfield at all. The super-soppers are doing their work. And the groundstaff is almost ready to peel off the main cover as well.








7.55pm  Astonishingly there's no rain 500 metres from the Stadium. The good news is the intensity of the shower has reduced. It's now a thin drizzle. 


7.45pm  A thin drizzle has turned into a sharp downpour. The covers are coming on. The forecast was for heavy rain in the evening. It's been threatening to pour for a couple of days now. It held up for much of the day, but the fluffy clouds have burst open. RCB were just beginning to build momentum, but they'll have to start all over again whenever play resumes.


There's been a lot of rumble around the city. Central Bengaluru was entirely dry until now. The expression on the faces of the fans tells you a story. They need this game to go the distance for that gives RCB the best chance of victory with that 18-run margin. CSK won't really mind this. A shortened game will be to their advantage. A washout means CSK go through to the playoffs.


Rangadham : "Hope the batters don't hit the ball to high. It may bring the clouds down."

works it to square leg

slapped wide of a diving Faf at mid-on! Timed nicely.

steered down to square third
the leading edge flies just over Swapnil's outstretched hands

Swapnil from around the wicket with his left-arm spin

shortish on middle, pulled to deep midwicket

whips this to wide long-on, Rahane wanted the second, Rachin wasn't keen
works it down to long-on as he churns strike back to the left-hander
slaps this to long-off, hit well but Maxwell comes around quickly
clean strike inside-out over extra cover, was hitting it with the spin so it was safe and sumptuous.

cut hard into the sweeper cover region, good work by Lockie Ferguson
tucks it to deep midwicket

pre_text: Ahmed: "RCB need wickets and need it soon! You don't want to see Dhoni there with 18 needed in 6 balls. He will take it home and become immortal!"

commentary: flays this to sweeper cover for a single
works this low full toss to deep midwicket

the slower delivery has done the trick! Lockie bowls a leg-cutter on a length, Rahane sees width and looks to go over cover but ends up slicing it to Faf at the edge of the ring at cover. It was a steepler but he made it look very easy. You'd think Rahane has done his job. Over to Dube & co now.

CSK need 116 off 11 overs to qualify


A reminder that you can also follow this high-profile and crucial game in Hindi right here.

Not sure what it was about, but Faf and Kohli just had a long chat with the umpires during the change of overs.

commentary: uppish but just wide of Kohli at short cover. Seems like the plan is to dig it in and trouble Dube with bounce
pre_text: Dube comes in as the Impact Player.

commentary: dug into the pitch again, Dube gets besides the line as he defends
excellent from Lockie as he cramps Dube up while also beating him for pace with that bumper. Dube was looking to arch back and ramp it wide of the keeper
cutter on a length, punched to deep cover
slower and fuller on leg stump, worked to long-on.
shot of a length around off, and pulled towards deep midwicket
pre_text: Hello again, everyone. And with me, I bring Maxwell back. From around to Ravindra.

commentary: ahh, this turns away off a length on middle, and hits Dube on the back pad as he is squared up and beaten while he looks to push
on a length on middle, and whipped to deep square
this is much fuller, and on off. Chipped towards long-off
ahh, on a fullish length just outside off, and quicker. Dube wanted to stab, but missed
shorter side of a length on the stumps, and clipped to deep midwicket
short of a length on leg, and nudged behind to fine leg
pre_text: CSK's required rate now zooming...

commentary: ohh, a head-high full toss, and four to beat short fine leg to his left! It is, naturally, called a no-ball. So it is a free hit. It landed just above his head, as Ravindra swivelled to pull and went off the top edge

six over deep midwicket! He got his front leg out of the way, and thumped this full toss arriving at stump height on middle and leg. The fielder leaped, but the ball went above his hands. Fifty for Ravindra too!
pre_text: Free hit. But before that, there is a lot of discussion between the umpires, and Kohli and du Plessis. Not sure what that was about, though.

commentary: ramped over short third! Ravindra giving the treatment to his New Zealand team-mate. Short of a length on fifth stump, and Ravindra rides the bounce before upper-cutting it
angles this length ball in around middle and off. Punched to deep point
pre_text: From around now

commentary: another dot ball to Dube, who is now on 4 off 10 balls. Short of a length at rapid pace on off, and punched to cover
ahh, Kohli is at short cover, and Dube finds him again, as he pushes at a shortish ball angling across towards the stumps
short of a length on leg, and Ravindra went to pull but his hit high on his body
pre_text: Rayen: "Dube, please rotate the strike if you can't hit it.. Don't pressurise Rachin"

commentary: chips this length ball towards extra cover, as long-off comes rushing forward. Du Plessis from cover moved and slid to his left too
dropped by Siraj! He came running and tumbling forward from long-on, as Dube heaved at this full ball on off, but top-edged it
goes swinging across the line, but gets an inside edge past the stumps
backs away, and thumps this full ball on off towards long-off

ahh, complete mix-up, and Ravindra is run-out! CSK could lose all the momentum with this wicket, not least because Dube is struggling. Ravindra called for two initially, and Dube responded. But just after turning back to attempted the second, Ravindra said no. By then, though, Dube was almost through at the non-striker's end. So Ravindra was out of his crease. This is what happened before: he got a length ball angling into his pads, which he whipped to deep square
short of a length banged outside off. Chopped towards cover
pre_text:
Green into the attack

commentary: uff, just short of Karthik! He dived to his left, but the ball brushed his glove and went away. Jadeja saw good bounce off a length on sixth stump, and went poking, getting an outside edge
pre_text: Jadeja at No. 6, with plenty of pressure on CSK

commentary: length ball angling across, and taking his pad as he looked to clip. The ball dribbled towards point, even as Dube was almost at the striker's end by the time Jadeja started

Dube's struggle ends! He falls for 7 off 15 balls, which is so many when you consider what is at stake. Green banged it on a back of a length at a change of pace, and got it to angle across towards middle and off. Dube, despite being as tall as he is, couldn't get the pull away. He found long-on instead, and had to depart
dismissal: S Dube c Ferguson b Green 7 (20m 15b 0x4 0x6) SR: 46.66

commentary: length ball outside leg. He looked to clip, but it was quite wide
pre_text: Santner in

driven wide of mid-off! Green went on a fullish length, and angled that across. The ball finished around off, and Jadeja timed the drive well
on a length just outside off, and pushed to point, where there is a fumble
pre_text: Siraj replaces Maxwell

commentary: short of a length on middle and off, and swat-pulled to deep midwicket
almost a yorker-length ball on fifth stump. Jammed to long-on

short_text: Mohammed Siraj to Jadeja, no run

skips down, and slaps this short-of-a-length ball around off to deep point on the bounce

wow, superb catch by du Plessis! Santner is left shocked, even as the RCB supporters are jumping with joy. Placed at mid-off, du Plessis flies a few above, and stretches his right hand across. It would make for a fantastic pic if someone might have captured it: the ball in du Plessis' hands, and du Plessis defying physics. Siraj bowled a low full toss on off, and Santner lofted, only for du Plessis to intervene
pre_text: Nimit: "A fabulous spell by Maxwell has gone under the radar"

fuller side of a length around fifth stump, and shaping in. Nudged back to the bowler

commentary: swivels at this shortish ball angling into his pads, and whips to fine leg to pick two

commentary: clips this length ball shaping in for a single to fine leg
short of a length on middle, and pulled off the top half of the bat behind square

flashed over long-off! He opens the face of the bat a bit, and goes over mid-off, who is inside the circle. The ball is a slower one from the back of the hand and on a full length outside off, as Jadeja went through the line

another short-of-a-length ball outside off, and swatted towards long-on

short of a length on middle, and he pulls but gets a bottom edge towards deep square leg

pre_text:
Dayal to Dhoni

Ashish Pant reporting that RCB seem behind the over rate. CSK need 17 to qualify. RCB need to keep CSK to at most 200, which means they can concede maximum 16.

commentary: slower ball... and Dhoni falls! Half the Chinnaswamy erupts out of joy; the other half wonders if they have seen Dhoni for the last time ever. Dayan bowls a length ball angling away towards off, but this is from the back of the hand. Dhoni goes hoicking across the line, but can hit it only as far as deep backward square leg. Who knows we may have seen the last of Dhoni on the field
